newsitem.title: GERMANY: CSFB to expand Frankfurt equities trading.
newsitem.headline: CSFB to expand Frankfurt equities trading.

text.p: Credit Suisse First Boston AG, the German unit of Swiss banking giant Credit Suisse, said on Thursday it planned to double the number of its equity dealers in Frankfurt to 12 as soon as possible.
The bank might also hire one or two more bond dealers in Frankfurt to add to its current team of eight, Thomas Amstutz, management board member of CSFB AG, told Reuters.
But it had ceased currency dealing in Frankfurt as part of a reorganisation in which it has based its European currency dealing activities in London and Zurich, Amstutz said.

"We plan to double our equities team, we will be 12 in equities trading," Amstutz said. CSFB had already hired three new traders who had not started yet, and was looking for a further three, Amstutz said.
"Our strategy is to strengthen equity trading in Germany. In that sense German was chosen as our first priority in continental Europe."
Amstutz reiterated the bank's denial of a report in German magazine Boerse Online this week which said CSFB planned to cease all its trading activities in Frankfurt.

Credit Suisse's German operations were merged with the German business of its investment bank unit CSFB on October 10 as part of the Swiss group's global reorganisation. The merged company is called CSFB AG.
